findings: New wave-2 template distilled from a recurring field workflow pattern; no prior library source existed for this solution.
The field pattern relied on live systems, runtime clocks or model-generated text, which cannot be replayed deterministically or shared publicly.
The field pattern included organization-specific names, records and identifiers that must not appear in a public template.
Write-shaped steps in the pattern (submit, file, send, approve) needed an explicit human gate.
fixes: Re-implemented the workflow as a stdlib-only single-file agent over a fixed fictional snapshot with one operation per story turn.
Replaced every name, record and identifier with invented data; boundary grep against the pattern sources returned zero hits.
Fixed the snapshot date and precomputed day counts so every output is deterministic.
Every write-shaped operation returns a draft, pre-check or recommendation and states that nothing was submitted, filed, sent or changed.
remaining_boundary: Production connections and all external actions require customer approval, least-privilege controls, and an authorized human workflow.
